name: IEC buffer element (rectangular form)
summary: Non-inverting IEC element marked 1, passing the input state to the output unchanged.
description: A rectangular element with the qualifier 1 and no negation simply repeats its input. It is used to show isolation between logic stages, a fan-out point, or an interface where a physical buffer device exists. When the buffer has greater than normal drive capability, an amplifier triangle pointing in the signal direction is added inside the outline.

On logic diagrams for control panels the buffer often marks where a signal leaves one card or module and enters another. Tagging the buffer with the module reference helps fault finding because it identifies the boundary at which the signal can be measured.
A plain 1 element says nothing about output type or enable. Three-state, open-collector and Schmitt variants each require an additional qualifier.
readingNotes: A buffer may exist only to show a module boundary; check the module tag.
Look for drive, three-state or open-circuit qualifiers next to the output.
drawingChecklist: Add the output qualifier where the output is not a normal push-pull stage.
Identify the physical device or module when one exists.
distinction: The same box with output negation is an inverter; the amplifier triangle inside marks increased drive capability.
